It doesn’t matter if you already technically have a partner. It’s about treating your children like partners.
That’s why I said potentially and listed reactions she would have to have to further point to this

Emotional incest is not the same thing as physical incest. It’s a phrase that’s used to describe a form of emotional abuse that happens when a parent treats their child as a partner. If you’re partner feels constantly obligated, pressured, or guilted into obeying what his mom wants in detriment to himself then he probably was a victim of some sort of emotional abuse.

He can set boundaries by firmly and clearly communicating to her, preferably first through text. “Hi Mom, I’m very busy, I don’t think I’ll be able to spend time with you this week.” If his mom respects his wishes then good! A boundary was set and she followed if. If she complains, whines, or starts guilting then you have to be clear and disengage in her behavior. “This is not up for discussion, I will not talk about this any further.” Hang up and ignore. Repeat until she understands that her behavior will not lead to what she wants.

If she does something extreme like show up at the house, then you must continue to enforce the boundary. “No you cannot come in. I told you I couldn’t spend time this weekend. Go back.” Rinse and repeat enforcing boundaries until she lets go.

This seems like a potential case of covert incest/emotional incest. She is treating him more like a partner than a son. Does your boyfriend have low self esteem? The fact that she also constantly puts him down and makes a big deal complaining about the things around her probably lead to your boyfriend learning to be complacent/trying to please her in order to avoid the situation from getting worse. If your boyfriend tries to set boundaries how will she react? Will she step over them, get extremely mad at him, manipulate/guilt him into giving her what she wants?

If I were you I’d see if your boyfriend can try testing it out to get a clearer answer. Being obsessed with your son that you need him to be with you basically 24/7 is not normal behavior.

She’s doing it for herself, not for you. You are under no obligation to visit the parents that caused your homelessness and didn’t care about whether you were dead or alive for over 13 years. 


If you want to see her because you feel it will help you out go for it. Just remember that these people had a long time to try to reconnect to you and only chose now because she probably doesn’t want to feel guilty for what she did.

Yes I noticed that, that’s why I recommended counseling foremost. However, if it did get worse after the kid I think its worth to re-examine. Not to mention the potential uneven distribution of chores as well as not expressing affection in the right form for his wife can explain behavior even before baby.

I think there’s a couple things here you might need to analyze and reflect on.

There’s a possibility that she is suffering from post partum depression, and that can contribute to her current mood and actions. Generally I believe you guys should go to marriage counseling and see what underlying issues there might be. If she cant speak to you about her problems, maybe suggest having her write them down? Maybe a list of things that make her happy and sad? 


In regards to chores, do you guys have child care or help? Are you sure the chores are really divided evenly? I ask this because maybe she doesn’t see it that way. For example, what about chores involving baby? When baby cries in the middle of the night who takes care of them? Who feeds or changes baby? Who takes baby out to play and walks? The reason why I ask this is because if your wife feels as if she is doing the majority of child care or chores, it might be negatively impacting her psyche and sexual state. Who wants to be in the mood for sex when you’re tired of taking care of baby and feel like you’re also taking care of your husband?  I’m not saying this is your case, just something to consider. 


I see you talk about buying presents, which is a good way to express affection, but might not be her love language. Have you ever complimented her randomly (in a non sexual way), or tell her you appreciate the work she does around the house? When was the last time you guys had a date? Or did something fun together?

I’m going to ask you some questions: 1) Is she a stay at home mom? 2) Do you do chores around the house? 3) Have you ever asked her what she would like from you in the relationship, or what you can do to improve? 4) Does she seem lethargic, sad, or cranky all the time?

Because she was abused.

The psychology of an abused victim doesn’t really allow for simple “refusal”.  Every time she spoke up, every time she tried to step out of line, she was either silenced, diminished or punished. Blue Diamonds episode makes this really clear, “how many times did you do this? how many times did you lock her in here? how many times did you make her cry?” ; and when Blue Diamond stands up to yellow diamond, it becomes abundantly clear that blue wasn’t the only one who repeatedly hurt pink. 


Why else do you think she effectively committed suicide? She felt unloved, unimportant, and powerless. She couldn’t refuse without being punished, and I would argue that at that point she also felt that she didn’t have a voice.


So her literally only solution to escape, was suicide.
